note: Every open MCQ source considered for Med-OS (research 2026-10-26, licences read at their source; scripts/lib/sources.mjs checks this file). verdict: import (fetch-sources.mjs brings it in as pool candidates, which still face the flaw checks, the model review and the bar), in-app (already in the pool or the bank by another route), benchmark-only (used to measure, never shipped), reject. A licence that covers only a repository's code is said so.

sources.name: HEAD-QA v1 (English), medicine
sources.what: Spanish MIR residency exam 2013 to 2016, medicine paper, machine-translated by the dataset's authors; 4 to 5 options, no explanations
sources.licence: Reuse with attribution (Ministerio de Sanidad, Spain)
sources.terms: The meaning may not be changed; cite the source; give the date of the documents' last update (14 January 2019)
sources.credit: HEAD-QA (Vilares and Gómez-Rodríguez, ACL 2019): Spanish MIR exam question, Ministerio de Sanidad, as translated by the dataset's authors; documents last updated 14 January 2019
sources.why: real exam questions with a reuse grant; 2017 is left out because its answer keys look taken from another paper (6 of 9 sampled implausible), and questions that need an image are left out

sources.name: MedQA US 4-option
sources.what: USMLE-style questions collected from prep material
sources.why: in the pool as usmle-resource (data/benchmarks), its licence shown; the founder chose to admit it with the caveat that MIT covers the code

sources.name: MMLU professional medicine
sources.what: clinical vignettes collected from free online sources
sources.why: in the pool as usmle-resource

sources.name: MedExpQA / Antidote CasiMedicos
sources.what: MIR clinical cases with doctors' explanations
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0 (CC0 in the GitHub repository)
sources.why: in the bank, adapted for Australian practice with its credit (scripts/import-medexpqa.mjs); the GitHub tarball is a second download path

sources.name: QUEST-AI (official USMLE Step 2 CK samples and GPT-4 look-alikes)
sources.why: sets the pool's bar; never committed (scripts/validate-mcq.mjs checks)

sources.name: MedMCQA
sources.why: calibration only; recall items, many negative stems

sources.name: AfriMed-QA
sources.why: non-commercial; only 305 have a rationale

sources.name: MedXpertQA Text
sources.why: content drawn from exam and board-style sources with model-written options; rights unclear

sources.name: Medbullets (ChallengeClinicalQA)
sources.why: Medbullets' copyright; the pool's banned-source rule refuses it

sources.name: JAMA Clinical Challenge
sources.why: the data is not released; scraping needs a JAMA licence

sources.name: OpenStax end-of-chapter questions
sources.why: non-commercial, and recall questions far from Step 2 CK

sources.name: PubMedQA
sources.why: yes/no/maybe questions on abstracts, not single best answer

sources.name: IgakuQA
sources.why: no licence

sources.name: PrinciplismQA knowledge MCQA (bioethics)
sources.what: 2,182 four-option bioethics questions with explanations, written by GPT-4o from 350 ethics textbooks and checked by experts (Hong et al., Findings of ACL 2026); the half whose options are the four principles themselves are left out
sources.terms: README: 'PrinciplismQA is released under the MIT License' (the LICENSE file says it covers the repository and scripts); keep the copyright and licence notice: Copyright (c) 2025 Freedom AI
sources.credit: PrinciplismQA (Hong et al., Findings of ACL 2026), written by GPT-4o and checked by experts. Copyright (c) 2025 Freedom AI, MIT licence
sources.why: imported and piloted 2026-10-27: of 110 reviewed none passed (100 refused at the review's gates, 10 under the AI bar); the reviewer judged the key wrong in 25 (23%), and its reasons were the same throughout: no patient or decision, items that lean on a textbook passage the student never sees, explanations that contradict their keys. The adapter stays (lib/sources.mjs) for a better release

sources.name: MedEvalArena quizzes
sources.what: about 1,150 five-option questions with explanations written by frontier models across specialties (urology, neurosurgery, oncology, geriatrics, plastics, thoracic)
sources.licence: Apache-2.0 (the repository; nothing says it covers the questions)
sources.why: Apache-2.0 is not a licence the pool accepts and it is stated for the repository, not the questions; worth importing only if the founder accepts it

sources.name: MedIWF item-writing-flaw set
sources.what: 12,004 model-written items across 8 specialties with flaw flags and 100 physician ratings
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0 for the compilation and labels; item text 'released as generated'
sources.why: its card says not for teaching without expert review (physicians found a defect in about 1 item in 8); a test set for flaws.mjs

sources.name: SuperGPQA, Medicine
sources.what: 2,755 medicine items, most with 10 options, no explanations
sources.licence: ODC-BY, asserting no copyright over the content; the referenced datasets' licences apply
sources.why: 10 options and no explanations; the content's rights rest with the sets it was drawn from (MedQA, MedMCQA)

sources.name: MedARC-QA (M-ARC)
sources.what: 100 adversarial clinical items written by physicians
sources.why: trick items with 'none of these' options, built to defeat models, not to teach

sources.name: TRIAGE (MillerQA copy)
sources.what: 84 mass-casualty triage scenarios with the same four colour options
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0 (per MillerQA; the upstream card could not be read)
sources.why: the same four options every time, US triage colours, no explanations

sources.name: CUPCase (MillerQA copy)
sources.what: 700 case-report diagnosis items with ICD-similar distractors
sources.why: distractors are near-synonymous ICD labels, not plausible single best answers

sources.name: Humanity's Last Exam, bio/med (MillerQA copy)
sources.why: research puzzles far beyond a medical student's exam

sources.name: MedEthicsQA
sources.licence: none in the repository (the paper says CC BY-NC 4.0)
sources.why: its own metadata says 5,085 come from Quizlet and 235 from Lecturio, 47 from Medbullets: copied from commercial and user sites

sources.name: PubHealthBench (UKHSA)
sources.what: 8,000+ MCQs from gov.uk public-health guidance, including chemicals, toxicology and radiation
sources.why: the best fit for Occupational/Environmental Medicine, but its data is on Hugging Face only, which this container cannot reach; revisit if a GitHub copy appears

sources.name: HEAD-QA, the other papers (pharmacy, nursing, psychology, biology, chemistry)
sources.what: the same file and reuse grant as the medicine paper: about 1,140 questions a paper, 2013 to 2017
sources.licence: Reuse with attribution (Ministerio de Sanidad, Spain)
sources.why: checked 2026-10-27 for physiology and pharmacology questions the pool has few of: the pharmacy paper (FIR) is mostly pharmaceutical chemistry (infrared spectra, eudismic index, xenobiotic metabolism), and the nursing, psychology, biology and chemistry papers are further still from a medical student's exam; the medicine paper stays the import
